tickets.description: The Foundation sentence reads 'As a result of the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC, Calif ... mistakenly published a video.' The time can modify the pre-announcement (oss-security relayed it at 20:22:51Z; php.net's feed says 20:32Z). The Register reads it as 'a couple of hours later' than 15:00; Feross says 'that evening'. The site (claim and timeline.json at 2026-10-20T20:00Z) presents 20:00 UTC as the video's time. Say 'evening of 20 October' or flag the ambiguity.

tickets.label: Finding-10
tickets.title: chainguard: Lorenc quote attributed to The Register is not in The Register
tickets.description: The note quotes Lorenc 'via The Register': 'I made the call to get these out early when exploits hit in the wild'. The Register capture has 'so we made the call to ship the fixes under that'. The quoted sentence appears only inside a Reddit comment embedded in the Foundation page ('but I made the call to get these out early when exploits hit in the wild.'), apparently quoting Lorenc elsewhere (likely Hacker News). Use The Register's words or capture the original.

tickets.label: Finding-11
tickets.title: no-exploitation: Time of the Austin interview is wrong: the post is 08:00 UTC (09:00 BST), not 08:00 BST
tickets.description: claims.json 'by' says '08:00 BST 22 October'; exploitation.json and timeline.json date it 2026-10-22T07:00Z. The capture's page.html JSON-LD gives the post datePublished 2026-10-22T08:00:23.293Z, and the rendered page (UTC browser) shows 'published at 08:00'. The vault's BBC notes.md is the origin of the BST error (the 07:55Z curl copy showed BST clock times, the Playwright capture shows UTC).

tickets.label: Finding-12
tickets.title: no-exploitation: Claim uses the BBC headline's absolute wording, not Austin's hedged words
tickets.description: Austin said "Not at the moment... it doesn't look like exploitation has taken off or been widespread", which allows some exploitation; 'There is no evidence yet that hackers have exploited the flaw' is the BBC's paraphrase. Reword to his words or attribute the headline to the BBC.

tickets.label: Finding-13
tickets.title: cisa-none: Claim drops CISA's own time qualifier
tickets.description: CISA says it 'has not observed exploitation ... as of the time of publication' (Release Date October 21, 2026, no time given). The claim text uses an undated present tense ('CISA has not observed exploitation'); the qualifier is only in the note. Put 'as of 21 October' in the claim itself, since Amazon, Cloudflare, watchTowr and NCSC NZ report exploitation attempts after that.

tickets.label: Finding-14
tickets.title: amazon-honeypot: The note narrows Amazon's sentence to honeypots; Amazon's text does not
tickets.description: Note: 'Attempts against honeypots, not compromises of victims'; history.json: "Amazon saying it is 'broadly exploited' against honeypots"; claims.json no-confirmed-compromise: "'broadly exploited' against sensors". Amazon writes 'we saw them used against our sensors almost immediately. PHP2Shell is now being broadly exploited in the wild.' and also 'With PHP2Shell, compromise may predate the advisory.' The honeypot limit is this site's reading. Say instead: Amazon gives no counts and names no victim; its evidence shown is honeypot telemetry.

tickets.label: Finding-15
tickets.title: probing: exploitation.json's Woodward row says Amazon's own post was not found
tickets.description: exploitation.json row (2026-10-22, Alan Woodward) has status 'reported; Cloudflare's own post confirms attack traffic, Amazon's own post not found' and cites thehackernews-php2shell-4days, while this claim (confirmed) cites aws-security-blog-madpot as Amazon's own confirmation.

tickets.label: Finding-16
tickets.title: latvia-attempts: 'none succeeded' overstates 'no reports of successful attacks so far'
tickets.description: CERT.LV: 'ta_u l_dz _im nav zi_u par sekm_giem uzbrukumiem' (but so far there are no reports of successful attacks), in the update of 21.10.2026 23:00 (20:00Z). exploitation.json words it correctly; claims.json does not. Reword and date it.

tickets.label: Finding-17
tickets.title: huntress-none: 'No public exploit code known' is dated before release, not 20:30 UTC on 21 October
tickets.description: The sentence 'we're not aware of public exploit code as of this writing' sits in the original pre-release section ('The fixes aren't out yet'), i.e. about 20 October. The claim and impact.json put it under 'as of 20:30 UTC on 21 October'. By then Amazon reports PoCs 'within hours' of release, CCCS says a PoC is available, and watchTowr reports PoC code on GitHub. Split the two halves and date each.

tickets.label: Finding-18
tickets.title: watchtowr-itw: Status 'unverified' understates the attempts half; the vault has four outlets quoting watchTowr
tickets.description: securityweek-first-attempts-sensors, securityweek-exploitation-days-before, darkreading-php2shell-red-alert and tenable-php2shell-faq (in data/sources.json) and therecord-php-warnings (vault only) quote Jake Knott: watchTowr sees in-the-wild exploitation attempts. Cite them and mark that half reported or corroborated.

tickets.label: Finding-19
tickets.title: watchtowr-itw: Claim omits watchTowr's own qualifier: no successful attempt, and sprayed exploits mostly do not work
tickets.description: Knott: 'Whilst nobody has been successful to date' (SecurityWeek) and 'The exploits being sprayed indiscriminately either don't work at all, test for timing-based differences, or crash the target'. Without this the claim reads as more than attempts.

tickets.label: Finding-20
tickets.title: kev-precedent: Status 'confirmed' outruns the weakest part (A2), and 'last PHP core RCE' is not shown
tickets.description: The one-day exploitation rests on one party (Akamai). The CVE record calls CVE-2024-4577 'Argument Injection in PHP-CGI' on Windows with certain code pages, a SAPI bug rather than the PHP core; and nothing captured shows it is the most recent PHP RCE (only that it is the most recent PHP entry in KEV). Say 'the last PHP flaw in KEV'.

tickets.label: Finding-21
tickets.title: kev-precedent: Honeypot attempts count as 'exploited in the wild' for 2024 but not for php2shell
tickets.description: Akamai's one-day evidence is exploit attempts against its honeypot network, the same kind of evidence as Amazon's MadPot hits, which the site's notes (amazon-honeypot, history.json) say are 'attempts against honeypots, not compromises'. Apply one standard to both.

tickets.label: Finding-22
tickets.title: affected-sites: Cited text capture no longer carries most of the list
tickets.description: The 08:05:59Z text capture (sha c88b8c5f...) has no mention of Edinburgh council, the BBC, online stores or the University of Geneva. The list is only in raw/page.2026-10-22T0755Z.html (summary bullet "Among the impacted sites are Wikipedia, Edinburgh council, many online stores and the BBC") and the Geneva item only in the header image alt text in raw/initial-data.json. The BBC dropped the bullet between 07:55Z and 08:05Z. The assessment should cite the raw file and its sha, and say the bullet was later removed.

tickets.label: Finding-23
tickets.title: affected-sites: Note "Not captured from any of the named organisations" is out of date
tickets.description: The vault holds operator captures: unige.ch returned HTTP 503 with an F5 "under maintenance" page at 2026-10-22 08:19:10Z (unige-site) and 08:19:43Z (ch-unige-down); nord.gouv.fr and rhone.gouv.fr served "Maintenance en cours" at 08:19:39-40Z; edinburgh.gov.uk was up (HTTP 200, normal homepage) at 08:19:03Z and 08:19:40Z; wikimediastatus.net showed "All Systems Operational" at 08:18:50Z. These show down/up state at capture time, not the reason. story.json repeats the out-of-date statement ("has not been captured from any of those organisations").

tickets.label: Finding-24
tickets.title: latvia-offline: Note "the one documented case ... from the agency itself" is contradicted by other site data and captures
tickets.description: The claim note and story.json call Latvia the one documented case of government services pulled from the public internet by the agency itself. The site's own nl-offline claim (status confirmed, "Primary statement") rests on Rijksoverheid saying NCSC.NL was taken offline "uit voorzorg"; EPFL's own homepage (epfl-site, 08:19:13Z) says it "has temporarily suspended access to some of its websites"; nord.gouv.fr and rhone.gouv.fr served maintenance pages at 08:19Z on 22 Oct.

tickets.label: Finding-25
tickets.title: latvia-offline: "Pulled from the public internet" overstates a geo-block
tickets.description: CERT.LV says access was restricted from abroad, selectively, and that residents accessing from Latvia should not be affected ("Paredzams, ka iedz_vot_jus, kuri valsts digit_lajiem pakalpojumiem piek__st no Latvijas, _ie ierobe_ojumi neietekm_s"). The note should say geo-blocked from abroad, not pulled from the public internet.

tickets.label: Finding-26
tickets.title: no-confirmed-compromise: Claim text lacks its as-of and scope
tickets.description: The negative holds only "in every captured source, as of the latest capture" (newest checked 2026-10-22T11:33Z). The note says so, but the claim and status "confirmed" read as a settled fact about the world. The supporting negatives are old: Huntress as of 20:30Z on 21 Oct, Imperva pre-disclosure only, CERT.LV 20:00Z on 21 Oct, against Amazon's "broadly exploited in the wild" and Cloudflare's "millions" of attempts. Suggest status "reported" or wording "No named organisation, in any captured source as of <stamp>, ...".

tickets.label: Finding-27
tickets.title: nl-offline: "Primary statement" covers only NCSC.NL
tickets.description: The Rijksoverheid capture names only NCSC.NL; DigiD, MijnOverheid and Overheid.nl are not in it, and dutchitleaders-websites-offline is a Cloudflare challenge (75 chars). Status "confirmed" with note "Primary statement" overstates three of the four services. Cite tpo-nl-digid-offline and insurancebusiness-uk-councils-met (DigiD, MijnOverheid) and reuters-factbox-websites-offline (Overheid.nl), and mark those parts reported.

tickets.label: Finding-28
tickets.title: nl-offline: "No signs of active exploitation of those services" is narrower than any source
tickets.description: Rijksoverheid says NCSC has not yet seen active misuse in general (13:59 on 21 Oct, before the patch); TPO quotes the minister saying there were "nog geen signalen" of active misuse. Neither speaks about those services specifically. Same wording in impact.json.

tickets.label: Finding-29
tickets.title: wikimedia-precaution: CNN does not carry the quoted phrase
tickets.description: The claim's "by" credits CNN, but CNN has only "precautionary measure" (told CNN on Thursday). The full phrase is in The Cyber Express, Newsweek (newsweek-php2shell-websites) and the Reuters factbox (reuters-factbox-websites-offline); cite those.

tickets.label: Finding-30
tickets.title: oxford: Quote is not in the cited source
tickets.description: oxfordchronicle-councils-offline (sha 35c84729...) does not contain the quoted words; only the collector's notes.md does. The words are in eadt-minister-budget-no-breach (sha 4c8556b5...), an embedded post signed "Oxford City Council (@OxfordCity) October 21, 2026". Cite that and change "via Oxford Chronicle"; impact.json also says Oxford Chronicle is "quoting" the councils' posts, which it is not.

tickets.label: Finding-31
tickets.title: uk-list: OBR is not in either cited source
tickets.description: Neither lbc-uk-websites-offline nor insurancebusiness-uk-councils-met mentions the Office for Budget Responsibility. It appears only in eadt-minister-budget-no-breach (PA), framing a question to the Scotland Secretary. Add that source or drop the OBR from this claim.

tickets.label: Finding-32
tickets.title: scale-70pc-websites: Cloudflare does cite its survey: the 70_ links to W3Techs
tickets.description: The claim note says 'None of the three cites the survey it comes from', numbers.json n-70-websites says 'Neither page names the survey', and a sections.json page says 'None of the pages that use it says how' it was measured. Cloudflare's rendered.html (capture 20261022T081216Z) hyperlinks '70% of websites' to https://w3techs.com/technologies/details/pl-php. The text.txt drops the link, which is likely why it was missed. OpenAI and Wiz do not cite a source.

tickets.label: Finding-33
tickets.title: scale-70pc-websites: The claim drops the survey's population qualifier
tickets.description: W3Techs' figure, as relayed by Tenable (69.3%) and Imperva (over 69%), is a share of websites whose server-side language is known, not of all websites. 'used by almost 70% of websites' overstates the population. numbers.json n-70-websites 'measures' describes the population correctly; the claim text should match.

tickets.label: Finding-34
tickets.title: scale-2.6m-hosts: 'of which' joins two different counters
tickets.description: The 2.6 million is VulnCheck's count; the 1.57 million unpatched is Censys's, out of the 2.58 million hosts Censys saw on 21 October (SecurityWeek). The same 'of which' framing recurs in questions.json and readings.json. Suggested wording: 'VulnCheck counts about 2.6 million; Censys saw 2.58 million on 21 October, of which 1.57 million were unpatched.'

tickets.label: Finding-35
tickets.title: scale-ncsc-nl: Confirmed: the inventory had 675 rows at cca173c64ec5, not 674; 4 not vulnerable, not 3
tickets.description: Counting table rows in raw/tree-cca173c64ec5/software/software_list_*.md gives 675 (Fix 46, Investigation 418, Vulnerable 206, Not vuln 4, blank 1). A fresh clone of raw/php2shell-cca173c64ec5.bundle (HEAD cca173c64ec5db92, 2026-10-22T10:40:58+02:00) gives the same 675 and its tree is identical to the vault's tree; the SPDX file software/spdx/PHP_Downstream_Inventory.spdx3.json has 675 software_Package elements and 4 NotAffected VEX relationships. The missing row is iBabs / iBabs bestuursportaal (Not vuln), in software_list_i.md, whose Links cell is empty, which is probably why the export parser skipped it. data/software.json (count 674, Not vuln 3) and raw/software-list-cca173c64ec5.json carry the error. This confirms BRIEF-CORRECTIONS.md v0.4.2.

tickets.label: Finding-36
tickets.title: scale-ncsc-nl: Site data disagree on the inventory count
tickets.description: data/claims.json (scale-ncsc-nl), data/numbers.json n-674 ('674 ... 3 Not vulnerable, 1 without a status'), data/software.json (count 674), questions.json, sections.json and index.md ('reaches 674 products') say 674; data/inventory-history.json self_check says the parser 'also finds 1 row the vault missed: iBabs'. numbers.json n-674 agrees with the claim but both are wrong against the file.

tickets.label: Finding-37
tickets.title: scale-ncsc-nl: The claim's status counts do not add up to its total
tickets.description: 206 + 46 + 418 + 3 = 673, not 674. The 674th row is 'The PHP Group / PHP core and Zend Engine', an unversioned anchor with no status. numbers.json n-674 mentions it; the claim does not. Corrected: 675 rows: 206 vulnerable, 46 fixed, 418 under investigation, 4 not vulnerable, 1 PHP-core anchor without a status.

tickets.label: Finding-38
tickets.title: disclosure-22oct: The BBC capture does not say the flaws were disclosed on 22 October
tickets.description: The claim's 'by' is 'BBC framing (UK morning coverage)', but the captured BBC live page (080559Z, and the 07:55Z raw copy) gives no disclosure date; it says details 'leaked online this week' and the patch 'has been rushed out'. Labelling a BBC statement 'contradicted' when the BBC did not make it misattributes. The '22 October' dates in the vault come from the original schedule (Foundation: 'from October 22nd, 14:00 UTC'), Wiz's thread ('Apply the Oct 22 security release') and ACSC's local time ('22 October 2026 at 0100 AEDT').

tickets.label: Finding-39
tickets.title: release-time: Three of the cited sources state a schedule, not a release time
tickets.description: php.net's pre-announcement and the oss-security relay say 'It is scheduled for ... 14:00 UTC'; CERT-FR says the publisher 'annonce la disponibilit_ des correctifs ... pour le 21 octobre 2026 _ 16h00 heure de Paris (14h00 UTC)'; the Foundation says it 'moved the release ... to October 21st, 14:00 UTC'. None of these observes the release. The 'by' line should read 'scheduled for 14:00 UTC' with Daubois as the one after-the-event statement.

tickets.label: Finding-40
tickets.title: preannounce-time: The Foundation's post gives two times for the pre-announcement
tickets.description: php-foundation-blog-security-release says 'published it at 19:30 UTC' and two paragraphs later 'the leak and pre-announcement around 20:00 UTC'. The note cites only the feed (20:32Z) and oss-security (20:22:51Z) against it; the source's own inconsistency should be shown.

tickets.label: Finding-41
tickets.title: fix-authored: Committer time is not the time a commit became public
tickets.description: 3584a98bd's committer date is 2026-10-21T16:06:22+02:00 (14:06:22Z). Git records when the commit object was made, not when it was pushed; and the release tags (13:35:38 UTC, pointing at release commit 136e049 dated 2026-10-19) already shipped the fix before 14:06. Suggested wording: 'committed to the branch at 14:06 UTC'.

tickets.label: Finding-42
tickets.title: offline-ncsc: LBC carried the same NCSC sentence on 21 October, before the NCSC page was modified
tickets.description: lbc-uk-websites-offline (dated '21 Oct 2026, 15:41', written before the release: 'Full details ... have yet to be published') quotes the NCSC verbatim with the BBC's wording. The NCSC page captured at 08:09Z on 22 Oct has HTTP last-modified 07:30:02 GMT that morning. Two outlets, one of them hours earlier than the BBC, quoting the same sentence suggests an earlier NCSC version said it and was reworded. The note frames it as a BBC misquote whose opening 'matches the Canadian CCCS text'; it should mention LBC and the likely supersession. The quote is not in the NCSC capture, so A3 stands until an earlier NCSC version is captured.

tickets.label: Finding-43
tickets.title: offline-allies: Italy's ACN does advise taking sites offline; the site says it does not
tickets.description: acn-it-php2shell text.txt (sha 19fac2ed..., line 70): 'Qualora non fosse possibile applicare tempestivamente gli aggiornamenti di sicurezza, si raccomanda di valutare di porre offline i siti e i servizi web che utilizzano versioni vulnerabili di PHP, sospendendone l'accessibilit_ fino all'avvenuto aggiornamento.' The claim note ('Italy ... give[s] no offline advice'), data/agencies.json (IT: offline 'none', 'Update only') and the collector notes ('NO offline or isolation advice') are all wrong against the same capture. agencies.json's offline_text 'Si raccomanda di aggiornare i prodotti vulnerabili.' is also truncated: the sentence continues 'seguendo le indicazioni dei bollettini di sicurezza riportati nella sezione Riferimenti.'

tickets.label: Finding-44
tickets.title: offline-allies: The BBC capture does not make the claim the site marks 'contradicted'
tickets.description: BBC (06:30 post): 'The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia, earlier urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes.' The offline sentence is then attributed to the NCSC only; the NSA appears in a separate post. The site's claim merges these into the BBC saying all four advise offline, and then marks that 'contradicted'. A reader is told the BBC was wrong about something it did not say.

tickets.label: Finding-45
tickets.title: offline-allies: Australia is not-shown, not contradicted, and the EU part largely holds
tickets.description: ACSC's page lists other actions and no offline advice, but its body text is stale (pre-patch) and absence on one page is not a contradiction. For 'the EU', CERT-EU advises isolating internet-facing applications from public networks, CERT-FR recommends isolating affected equipment, ACN advises taking sites offline, and CERT.LV says systems that cannot be updated must have internet access restricted. Only NCSC-NL, ENISA's CNW page and JPCERT give no such advice.

tickets.label: Finding-46
tickets.title: waf-nine-hours: 'Hours before disclosure' is shown only for Cloudflare, and Fortinet's date is after disclosure
tickets.description: The lead clause applies to all five vendors, but only Cloudflare states a time before the release. Imperva says protection was verified and monitoring began 'before the announcement' with no time; Akamai and Fastly posts are dated 21 October with no time; Fortinet's FortiWeb article was created 10/22/2026 07:55 AM (timezone not stated) and its signatures are 'in Alert Only mode' by default. Suggested: 'Cloudflare from 03:02 UTC on 21 October; Imperva before the announcement; Akamai and Fastly on 21 October; Fortinet signatures by 22 October.'

tickets.label: Finding-47
tickets.title: waf-nine-hours: The note's 'every vendor says ... patch anyway' is not carried for Fortinet
tickets.description: Cloudflare ('Customers should patch their PHP repos even with WAF protections'), Akamai ('The most effective defense continues to be the prompt application of vendor patches'), Fastly ('assume active mitigation will only serve as partial protection') and Imperva carry it. The Fortinet KB article gives signature and custom-rule steps and does not call them a stopgap or tell readers to patch.

tickets.label: Finding-48
tickets.title: rce-fpm: Status 'disputed' understates a claim the PHP advisory record carries; the dispute is about which CVE, not whether
tickets.description: GHSA-6wmf and openwall 2026/10/21/7 (PHP security team, CVE-2026-109619) both say unauthenticated RCE was demonstrated against PHP-FPM. Only the attribution to CVE-2026-109618 is in doubt. Suggest rewording to 'RCE is confirmed on PHP-FPM for CVE-2026-109619 (session upload progress path, needs a suitable application operation); for CVE-2026-109618 the advisory says no complete FPM exploit' and setting the status accordingly. Also cite openwall-oss-security-2026-10-21-7, which is in the manifest but not on this claim; the cited openwall 21/6 is the 109618 post and does not carry the claim.

tickets.label: Finding-49
tickets.title: rce-fpm: Glossary short text for PHP-FPM says 'whether a full exploit exists is disputed'
tickets.description: data/glossary.json (id fpm) short: 'Susceptible; whether a full exploit exists is disputed.' The PHP advisory GHSA-6wmf and oss-security 21/7 say FPM RCE was validated/demonstrated for CVE-2026-109619. The long text is accurate ('for the first flaw'); the short text misleads.

tickets.label: Finding-50
tickets.title: versions-old: 'from 5 onwards' is wider than the finder's '_= 5.4', and the 5.x sources look like echoes of the leak
tickets.description: Wiz (X post and blog) says 5.4 and later. NCSC-NL's text is the pre-patch banner ('vermoedelijk ... in ieder geval vanaf versie 5'), CERT-FR lists 'toutes versions 6.x' (PHP 6 never shipped; Daubois says watchTowr named 5, 6, 7 and 8), and The Hacker News says the HN leak claimed 'from PHP 5 onward'. These trace to one origin (A3 at most). Suggest the claim say '5.4 onwards per Wiz; PHP's backports imply 7.4 onwards'.

tickets.label: Finding-51
tickets.title: waf: Status 'disputed' understates: the sources agree a WAF is partial protection
tickets.description: CISA: 'may provide some protection'; BACS: 'alone is not sufficient'; Cloudflare: 'Customers should patch their PHP repos even with WAF protections providing an additional layer of defense-in-depth mitigation.' These are the same position at different emphasis. Suggest 'confirmed' as CISA's advice, with the BACS and Cloudflare caveats in the note.

tickets.label: Finding-52
tickets.title: pocs-wrong: Huntress is cited but does not carry the claim
tickets.description: The Huntress capture says it had 'not built or reproduced a proof of concept' and was 'not aware of public exploit code as of this writing'; it says nothing about VulnCheck or a 200 response. The 'by' field names Huntress too. Remove it or cite what it actually says.

tickets.label: Finding-53
tickets.title: ac-high: Status 'confirmed' on a claim whose first half is a reading
tickets.description: 'Triggering the bug is much easier than turning it into code execution' is Imperva's characterisation (verbatim, unquoted on the site). A reading caps at A3. Split the claim: the AC:H record is confirmed; the ease comparison should be shown as Imperva's reading (with Fastly agreeing).

tickets.label: Finding-54
tickets.title: more-paths: Missing context: the fix removed the OOM bailout itself, not only the demonstrated paths
tickets.description: The fix commit replaces bailout on OOM with UnwindExit and GHSA-w8hw says 'The patch removes longjmp() for OOM'. Fastly's point still applies to bailout on other fatal conditions (timeouts, uncaught errors), which GHSA-6wmf calls 'conditional', but a reader could take the claim to mean PHP only patched the demonstrated paths. Say which bailouts remain.

tickets.label: Finding-55
tickets.title: more-paths: Note leans on an unconfirmed report PHP reportedly rejected
tickets.description: 'consistent with the Fediverse report of a third bug' cites the oss-security thread, which is an unnamed second-hand report, and the same thread says Canonical was told by PHP it is 'unrelated and not a real issue'. The thread does not carry Fastly's position and should not be cited as support.

tickets.label: Finding-56
tickets.title: ac-high: 2 smaller precision and sourcing points
tickets.description: Fastly quote drops the quotation marks around 'safe': Capture: 'most deployments may be _safe_ from RCE.' The site drops the scare quotes, which changes the tone: Fastly is hedging the word. | Imperva phrase used without attribution in the claim text: The claim's first clause is Imperva's sentence word for word; it should be quoted and attributed.

tickets.label: Finding-57
tickets.title: affected-sites: 1 smaller precision and sourcing point
tickets.description: "Online shops" rests on the BBC alone and is vague: No capture names an online shop taken offline; the BBC capture otherwise mentions online shops only as platforms PHP powers. The University of Geneva item comes from an EPA photo alt text, not reporting text.

tickets.label: Finding-58
tickets.title: ahead-of-attackers: 1 smaller precision and sourcing point
tickets.description: Amazon's 17 October attempt is second-hand: The 17 October MadPot attempt is known only from CJ Moses 'in a post shared with The Hacker News'; no Amazon post is captured.

tickets.label: Finding-59
tickets.title: ai-found: 2 smaller precision and sourcing points
tickets.description: 'frontier' is not Calif's word: Calif writes 'No special harness, or access to models that weren't generally available to everyone were used in the initial bug discovery' and refers to an 'LLM companion'. 'Frontier AI' is Wiz's and OpenAI's language, not Calif's. | Calif's model is named only second-hand: That Calif used GPT-5.6 Sol rests on OpenAI's blocked blog (openai-blog-coordinated-disclosure text.txt is 0 bytes) and press relays (cybernews, wikipedia). Calif's own page names no model.

tickets.label: Finding-60
tickets.title: amazon-honeypot: 2 smaller precision and sourcing points
tickets.description: 'from multiple actors' is stated as fact; Amazon says 'suggesting': Amazon: 'The actual payloads and choices in anonymization infrastructure varied, suggesting these were multiple actors.' Use 'probably from multiple actors'. | Only one capture of Amazon's post, 21 hours after its date: The post is dated 21 Oct with no time; the single capture is 11:17Z on 22 Oct. The Hacker News (captured 08:13Z) already reports 'broad exploitation in the wild', so the sentence existed by then, but whether it was in the first version cannot be shown.

tickets.label: Finding-61
tickets.title: cf-millions: 1 smaller precision and sourcing point
tickets.description: Name the missing method, and set against Imperva's pre-disclosure zero: Thousands of attempts in the 10 hours before announcement (Cloudflare) and no matching traffic in pre-disclosure monitoring (Imperva, claim imperva-none) are different populations and probably different signatures; the site should say so where both appear.

tickets.label: Finding-62
tickets.title: chainguard: 1 smaller precision and sourcing point
tickets.description: Notification timing differs between relays: The Register: Lorenc 'notified the PHP coordinated disclosure channel about his plans' (before). Feross: 'he notified the group right after making the call'. Feross's post ID 2113043398664015878 decodes to 2026-10-21T23:02:59Z, so the source's published '2026-10-22' is off by a day in UTC.

tickets.title: Front page: 'Websites on PHP 8.1 or older have no ready-made fix' is contradicted by the source it cites
tickets.description: data/plain.json, facts. The php.net advisory (php-net-advisory, cited) says: 'Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details'. The PHP project itself ships no release for 8.1 and older, and its minimal source backports for 7.4 to 8.1 are not packages; but distributions and LTS vendors do ship ready-made packages. Say: 'PHP itself has no release for 8.1 or older; your Linux distribution or LTS vendor may have one'.
